info.name: Level 2 – Layered Payment Platform
info.description:
HTTP API of `levels/02-layered-architecture`.

**Start first** (from the repo root):
```
./mvnw -q install -DskipTests
./mvnw -q exec:java -pl tools/provider-simulators   # ports 4101–4107
./mvnw -q spring-boot:run -pl levels/02-layered-architecture   # :8080
```
Run the folders in order (or the whole collection with the Runner). Ids from each response (`paymentId`, `attemptId`, `paypalOrderId`) are stored in collection variables by a collection-level test script. `X-Merchant-Id` says who calls; money-moving commands get a fresh `Idempotency-Key` (`{{$guid}}`) unless the request demonstrates replay.

exec: // Runs after EVERY request: remember ids from payment responses so later requests can use them.
// PayPal-like sim: the approval link carries the order id

item.name: 0. Setup
item.description: Reset every simulator, so earlier fault injections don't leak into this run.

item.name: 1. Authorize → capture → refund (Stripe, manual capture)
item.description: FLOW A then FLOW B. `acme` is routed to Stripe by the `by-merchant` rule. Manual capture holds the money first; capture takes part of it; refunds give it back. Run the requests in order.

item.name: Refund the rest (empty body = everything refundable)

request.description: Every PaymentEvent recorded by the aggregate, with its actor.

item.name: 2. Cancel an authorization
item.description: Release held money instead of capturing it.

item.name: 3. Automatic capture
item.description: `capture: automatic` authorizes and captures in one call.

item.name: 4. Customer action (PayPal approval)
item.description: "Requires customer action" is an explicit outcome, never hidden in the adapter. `globex` + GBP routes to PayPal (by-currency rule). The PayPal-like sim needs the buyer to approve, simulated by its `/sim/orders/{id}/approve` endpoint.

item.name: 5. Routing (merchant → currency → default)
item.description: Which provider gets the payment. Each response's `provider` field shows the routing decision.

item.name: hooli EUR, refundsRequired → a provider that can refund

request.description: `refundsRequired: true` adds Capability.REFUND to the requirements, so the router skips providers that can't refund.

item.name: pied-piper → chargeonly (direct charge, captured at once)
vandelay → asyncpay (202 processing, result comes later)
6. Idempotency-Key
item.description: Money-moving commands need an `Idempotency-Key`, scoped to merchant + path. Same key + same body replays the stored answer; same key + different body is a client bug.

item.name: First request with a fixed key
Same key, same body → same answer replayed
8. Faults, fallback and reconciliation
item.description: Fault injection on the simulators. A timeout means OUTCOME UNKNOWN: the platform must NOT fall back to another provider (that could double-charge); reconciliation resolves it later by asking the provider about our attempt id. Errors that prove nothing was charged (503) are safe to fall back on.

request.description: Simulator control endpoint: the next 1 business request(s) to this simulator fail with `decline`.
Simulator control endpoint: the next 10 business request(s) to this simulator fail with `http-503`.

item.name: globex EUR → adyen 503 → falls back to stripe

request.description: Fallback order is [adyen, stripe]. 503 proves no charge happened, so fallback is safe.

exec: pm.test('two providers tried', () => pm.expect(new Set(pm.response.json().attempts.map(a => a.provider)).size).to.eql(2));

item.name: Stripe: next request times out (charges, never answers)

request.description: Simulator control endpoint: the next 1 business request(s) to this simulator fail with `timeout`.
Takes ~3 s (read-timeout). The money MAY have moved, so the status is `unknown`.

item.name: Stripe sim ledger (was the customer charged?)

request.description: Same as the scheduled job (every 30 s): looks up unknown payments by attempt id.

item.name: 9. Webhooks (signed by Postman)
item.description: FLOW C. One endpoint, `POST /webhooks/{provider}`. The pre-request scripts sign each body with the same HMAC scheme as the provider's verifier, using the secrets from application.yml. The provider echoes OUR attempt id, which is how the payment is found.

request.description: Simulator control endpoint: the next 1 business request(s) to this simulator fail with `async`.

exec: // Sim-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex hmac_sha256(secret, t + "." + body)>
// The body is resolved first: the signature must cover the exact bytes that are sent.

item.name: Same Stripe event again → 200 (deduplicated by the inbox)

exec: // Sim-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex hmac_sha256(secret, t + "." + body)>
// The body is resolved first: the signature must cover the exact bytes that are sent.
// Signed with the WRONG secret: the platform must answer 401 and store nothing.

request.description: Simulator control endpoint: the next 1 business request(s) to this simulator fail with `async`.
CHECKOUT.ORDER.APPROVED is not about payment state: verified, stored, acknowledged.
